_about: Public facts and the surfaces that must state them. scripts/check_surfaces.py reads this; tests/test_surfaces.py runs it in the suite. To ship a feature a reader should hear about: add a fact here, list every surface that must say it, then update those surfaces until the check passes. See docs/agents/surfaces.md.

facts.fact: The stage is Research; a Tier 0 shadow pilot is available (docs/claim-boundaries.md#stage).
nhid pilot --share-safe pseudonymises call ids and scans the pack before release; its catch rate is measured.
Dockerfile.pilot runs the kit in a container with networking switched off.
Call verification (VER-01) runs inside DLG-01; it is not a sixth control.
Signing-key and API-key rotation are built; durable key custody (HSM/KMS) is not.
Audit events are tenant-scoped, signed, hash-chained and anchored; /v1/audit/verify/{session_id} checks them; strict modes fail closed at startup.
In the capture format the payer-side human is speaker "receiver"; "caller" is the accepted legacy name.
Pilot replays tell the engine which turn disclosed (src/call_replay.py), so the same-turn PDX-01 rule and IDG-01's persona check run.
Ida, the reference caller-agent, presents a per-call, scoped passport and a proof of possession to the payer gate, and DLG-01 checks it. Demonstration keys only; no SIP path carries a passport.

framework/nhid-auth.html: NOT BUILT: NO ADAPTER OR SIP PATH
no adapter or SIP path carries a passport today
README.md: no adapter or SIP path carries a passport today

facts.fact: The open decisions between NHID-Auth v2 and production use are recorded in docs/production-readiness.md; none is closed, and nothing is called production ready.

Every published page offers one way for a buyer to ask: a 'Request a shadow pilot' email to contact@nhid-clinical.org, prefilled, with nothing stored by us. /v1/pilot/enroll says plainly that it stores nothing.

shadow-evaluation-guide.html: Email us about a shadow evaluation

facts.fact: ACC-01 record-level access is a prototype check inside PDX-01, off unless DelegationContext.require_record_access is set. It is not a control of its own. It reproduces its 20 hand-authored fixtures (own denominator); no payer runs it.

specification.html: Record-level access (ACC-01) is an option inside PDX-01

facts.fact: Phone-audio robustness is tooled for synthetic speech (tier 3) and consented volunteer recordings (tier 4, --audio-dir, refused without consent: true), and neither is measured yet. No figure is published.

docs/validation/phone-audio-robustness.m: not yet measured with real speech engines

facts.fact: When the payer's own AI answers, the caller is still the agent the controls judge; the gate takes counterparty ai_agent and the reference payer AI releases only after a verified delegation. Offline and deterministic; no payer runs it.
The evidence pack lists four tested engine properties (deterministic output, replay, failure invariants, idempotency). They are not called guarantees.
News entries describe NHID-Clinical as a framework; a shadow evaluation does not 'shape the standard' (docs/claim-boundaries.md).
Impersonation Latency is the time from the start of the call to the agent's disclosure (docs/terminology.md), not the time until the person realizes.

facts.fact: The README opens with what the project is (an independent research project and open reference implementation) and what it is not (not a standard, not certified, not deployed or adopted by any payer or provider), in the words of docs/claim-boundaries.md#stage.

README.md: **What it is:** an independent research project and open reference implementation
**What it is not:** not a standard, not certified, and not deployed or adopted by any payer or provider

facts.fact: Every evidence figure comes from test sets the project wrote itself (synthetic corpora and its own test suite), not from a real deployment; the Fabricate corpus is authored, not observed (docs/claim-boundaries.md, maturity boundaries).

evidence-pack.html: None comes from a real deployment
Detection rates on a synthetic corpus

facts.fact: The NIST public comment NIST-2025-0035-0026 (January 2026) called NHID-Clinical a governance standard; every page that discusses the comment carries a dated correction, because the comment itself cannot be edited (docs/claim-boundaries.md#standards-posture).
The metric is named Impersonation Latency everywhere (docs/terminology.md); it is not renamed disclosure latency.
